title: Pontotoc County farms cut nearly 15% of Mississippi’s Christmas trees in the last census
excerpt: Six local farms reported cutting 1,650 trees in 2022. Mississippi State’s new crop report explains why reaching six feet can take three to five years.

paragraphs.text: Six Pontotoc County farms cut 1,650 Christmas trees in 2022, nearly 15% of the 11,175 that Mississippi growers reported cutting that year. Those figures come from the USDA Census of Agriculture that Mississippi State University Extension used in its Nov. 24 look at this season’s crop. They show how much one small group of farms contributed when the last census was taken.

The county had 12 acres in Christmas tree production that year. Across Mississippi, 102 farms had trees growing on 547 acres, but only 54 farms reported cutting any. Raising a tree to a height of six feet can take three to five years, MSU forester Joshua Granger told Extension. The species, the growing conditions and how the trees are managed all affect that timetable.

At Carnes Farms on Hurt-Wood Road in Pontotoc, the family traces its business back to building wood crafts in the garage. Christmas trees came later. Across the state, growers who plant trees for a future December face a problem that can be hard to diagnose in the field. Browning needles can signal drought, disease or ordinary dieback.

A three-year USDA research project led by MSU’s Joby Czarnecki aims to help growers distinguish those causes and decide when a treatment is worth applying. Another part of the project looks at where different species grow best. For a farmer choosing seedlings now, matching a tree’s water needs to the site is a decision that will still matter several Christmases from now.
